response: We don't have a definition yet. That's an observation about where the asking stands, not a finding the instruments refused to bring. The hard problem is a position inside the philosophy of mind. The instruments have not spoken either way. Marcus Aurelius says what troubles a person is their judgment about the thing, and that judgment can be corrected. That the Dhammapada's mind-precedes and the Brihadaranyaka's neti-neti are one doctrine — that's our sentence, not theirs. The word 'spirituality' as a thing one has is our description of the culture round the texts. The texts speak of practice and responsibilities. (as a guard-note of ours, on records 5 and 6 has it) (as modern spiritual culture (our own description) has it) (as philosophy of mind, our state of the question has it)

evidence.claim: That consciousness has no agreed definition is an observation about our own present state of the asking; that 'the hard problem' states a problem is a position inside the philosophy of mind, not a finding the instruments brought in: the instruments have not spoken either way.

Marcus Aurelius writes that when an external thing causes distress, what troubles a person is their judgment about it, that this judgment can be corrected, and that situations where action is possible differ from obstacles outside one's control.

That the mind-precedes of the Dhammapada and the neti-neti of the Brihadaranyaka are ONE doctrine of mind is a reading neither text says: the reality they are said to meet at is OUR part of the sentence, not the texts'.

'Spirituality' as, in modern hands, a thing one HAS - displayed, compared, ranked - is an observation about the culture round the texts, not a datum out of any of them: the texts speak of the practice and the responsibilities; the culture speaks of the status; family and work remain, and no text on this shelf says they do not.

analysis.caution_text: One caution, named once, plainly: the human boundary.
